title: USB-Powered Indoor Desk Temperature Display
brief:
A USB-powered indoor desk temperature display. Use an ESP32 DevKit board, BME280 breakout and 3.3 V compatible OLED, plus USB supply/cable and enclosure. Exact module variants, pinouts, current ratings, material and fit are unknown. Proposed outer enclosure 100 × 60 × 30 mm. Show changing temperature readings; compare to an independent reference. steps.title: Prepare Components
steps.detail: Gather all parts: ESP32 DevKit, BME280 breakout, OLED, enclosure, USB cable. Verify compatibility with 3.3V logic.

steps.title: Fabricate Enclosure Mounting
steps.detail: Drill or cut mounting holes for board, sensor, and display. Ensure internal space allows for wiring and heat dissipation.

steps.title: Wire Sensor and Display to Board
steps.detail: Connect sensor and display to ESP32 using defined I2C and power lines. Use soldering for secure connections.

steps.title: Upload Firmware
steps.detail: Program ESP32 to read sensor data and update OLED display. Use Arduino IDE or similar. Test via serial monitor.

steps.title: Assemble Enclosure
steps.detail: Insert all components into enclosure. Secure with screws or glue. Ensure USB cable entry point is accessible.

steps.title: Test Temperature Display
steps.detail: Power on device and verify that temperature readings update and display correctly. Compare to known reference (e.g., thermometer).
